name: Electrochemical Dissolution Sprayer EDS-2 'Lacquer'
description:
The EDS-2 generates a fine aerosol of electrochemically activated solvent compounds by passing a base liquid reagent through a high-voltage ionization grid immediately before ejection. The ionization process transforms the reagent from an inert transport medium into a highly reactive dissolution agent that aggressively attacks both organic polymers and biological lipid membranes. The spray itself is nearly invisible — a faint iridescent shimmer in direct light — making it exceptionally difficult to detect in dimly lit environments until contact is made.

What makes the EDS-2 distinctively dangerous is the selectivity of its ionization profile. By adjusting the voltage gradient on the ionization grid via a thumb dial on the grip, operators can tune the reagent's reactivity toward organic tissue, synthetic materials, or a balanced blend of both. At maximum organic setting, it strips exposed skin and mucous membranes within seconds; at maximum synthetic setting, it dissolves polymer armor coatings, adhesives, and certain cybernetic housing materials. The mixed setting is considered the most tactically versatile but produces a caustic byproduct fog that requires the operator to wear sealed respiratory protection.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the EDS-2 ostensibly as an industrial decontamination tool for hazardous polymer environments, and it remains technically legal as such in several GLMZ jurisdictions — a loophole that has made it a favorite of operators who need plausible deniability on weapon checks. The weapon is recognizable by its wide conical nozzle, dual reagent tanks (one base liquid, one ionization catalyst), and the faint electrical crackling audible during active discharge.
legality: Restricted (licensed industrial use only; unlicensed carry Prohibited)
specifications:
effective range: 2–12 meters (aerosol cone)
dispersal angle: 15-degree cone
reagent capacity: Base tank: 400ml / Catalyst tank: 200ml
ionization voltage: 8,000–14,000V adjustable
tuning modes: Organic (O-mode), Synthetic (S-mode), Mixed (M-mode)
continuous discharge duration: Approximately 22 seconds per full tank
weight: 4.2 kg loaded
operator protection required: Sealed respiratory mask recommended in M-mode
dimensions: 44cm overall, 18cm nozzle assembly
tactical_use: Operators use the EDS-2 to strip defensive advantages from targets before engagement — dissolving armor polymer coatings, removing adhesive traps, or degrading cybernetic housing to expose internal components. In close-quarters situations, the organic setting is used as a disabling tool: even brief facial exposure causes involuntary eye closure and severe respiratory distress, forcing targets out of cover. Industrial sabotage specialists use the synthetic setting to destroy equipment without leaving ballistic evidence. The aerosol's near-invisibility makes it effective as a trap layer in ventilation systems.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's corporate espionage circles, being 'lacquered' has become slang for having your defenses methodically stripped before a hostile move — professional, financial, or physical. The EDS-2's industrial licensing loophole is an open secret, and Zheng-Dao Bioelectric has never publicly acknowledged the weapon applications of the device, maintaining a posture of corporate innocence while quietly supplying the gray market. Operators who carry it are often perceived as precise and methodical rather than aggressive — the weapon suggests patience.
known_users: Corporate sabotage specialists and competitive intelligence operatives
'Varnish' — an anonymous fixer known for leaving dissolved equipment as a calling card
Hazardous materials workers who have quietly modified their units
story_hooks: A series of corporate equipment failures across competing firms all show signs of selective polymer dissolution. No ballistic evidence, no witnesses. Someone with an EDS-2 and an industrial license is running a quiet sabotage campaign.
A player is approached by a Zheng-Dao Bioelectric liaison who offers a significant payout to recover a specific EDS-2 unit — serial number provided. They won't say why that specific unit matters.
The players need to get through a door sealed with military-grade polymer adhesive. Someone mentions they know where to acquire a licensed decontamination sprayer.

A victim is found with dissolution injuries inconsistent with any known acid or solvent — the pattern suggests an ionized aerosol. The only legal holders of EDS-2 units in this district are three licensed industrial workers, all of whom have airtight alibis.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist sprayer device with an oversized conical nozzle dominating the front — appears part industrial decontamination equipment, part bioweapon. The wide, flared nozzle gives it an aggressive, predatory silhouette. Dual cylindrical tanks sit behind the nozzle like vestigial organs, connected by visible electrochemical plumbing. The overall impression is utilitarian menace: something designed to dissolve rather than pierce.
physical_description.dimensions: 44cm overall length; 18cm conical nozzle assembly; 12cm width across tank cluster; 8cm depth at grip
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-heavy when loaded — approximately 4.2kg distributed unevenly toward the nozzle assembly. Requires two-hand operation or braced single-hand grip. The weight feels deliberate, suggesting serious chemical payload rather than elegant engineering.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum frame; reinforced polymer composite tank housings (chemical-resistant); stainless steel nozzle assembly with ceramic ionization grid insert
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte gunmetal gray with deliberate wear patterns; the nozzle shows heat-stress discoloration (faint brown oxidation rings where ionization has scorched the ceramic). Tank housings have a satin finish with faint factory labeling still visible beneath wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte industrial gray with gunmetal accents; faint amber/copper electrochemical scorching around nozzle interior; minimal corpo branding in dark red (Zheng-Dao house color)
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with raised grip panels for gloved operation; textured surface is slightly tacky (chemical residue sealed into texture). Thumb dial for voltage tuning is hard plastic with minute numeric gradients (O/S/M markings visible in wear)
distinctive_features: Wide conical nozzle with visible ceramic grid interior (faint blue-white when powered)
Dual transparent reagent tanks with fluid level indicators — base tank larger than catalyst tank
Visible electrochemical conduit tubing connecting tanks to nozzle (thin, flexible, heat-marked)
Thumb-dial voltage adjuster on grip with three labeled positions (O / M / S) — dial shows wear from repeated tuning
Faint electrical crackling audible during idle (high-voltage capacitor hum just below hearing range)
Small exhaust vent on lower frame (ionization byproduct outlet)
Weathered Zheng-Dao Bioelectric stamp on left tank housing with serial plate (worn but legible)
Faint iridescent residue staining on nozzle interior (evidence of reactive aerosol contact)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric emblem (stylized electromagnetic coil within circle) stamped in dark red on upper left tank; serial plate recessed into grip (alphanumeric code worn to illegibility); 'INDUSTRIAL DECONTAMINATION DEVICE' stenciled in small white text on tank housing (faded)
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but battle-worn; field operators keep nozzle clean to prevent residue buildup, but the device shows consistent evidence of active use — scuffed grip, faint chemical etching on frame, heat stress marks on nozzle interior. Never pristine, always operational.

image_prompt: Industrial electrochemical sprayer mounted on tactical display stand, angled 45 degrees to show conical nozzle and dual reagent tanks. Dramatic side-lighting with blue-tinted accent light on nozzle interior to hint at ionization grid. Dark matte surface beneath (industrial concrete texture). Gloved operator hand gripping device, thumb poised on voltage dial. Faint wisps of iridescent aerosol mist suspended in light around nozzle cone — nearly invisible but shimmering. Emphasize worn metal, chemical residue staining, and military-industrial aesthetic. Zheng-Dao branding visible on tank. Cyberpunk gray-and-copper color grading. Gritty, utilitarian GLMZ-era manufacturing quality. --ar 3:2 --v 6
